claims.text: CALPHAD-based high-throughput computational screening can predict phase equilibria in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput screening can guide microstructure refinement in high-entropy alloys.
CALPHAD-based high-throughput screening can optimize properties in high-entropy alloys.
The initial Al–Cr–Fe–Mn–Ti alloy is in a disordered solid-solution state.
CALPHAD combined with high-throughput calculations can screen a multicomponent compositional space.
The method can predict phase stability and microstructural evolution under intended processing and operating conditions.
Calculations should cover relevant composition ranges and temperatures, including processing and service conditions.
Efficient computing resources are useful for handling the high computational load of high-throughput CALPHAD calculations.
The predicted stable primary solid-solution phase mediates microstructure refinement and property optimization.
Coherent precipitates such as L2₁ enhance alloy strength.
CALPHAD relies on computational software and thermodynamic databases.
High-entropy-alloy screening can use mixing enthalpy, mixing entropy, atomic-size difference, valence-electron concentration, and related physicochemical criteria.
CALPHAD predicts phase diagrams from thermodynamic databases and physicochemical criteria.
CALPHAD predictions enable controlled precipitate formation that refines the microstructure.
Controlled phase and precipitate formation can tailor mechanical and physical properties.

Alloys designed by this method will have improved operating-temperature phase stability, more refined and homogeneous microstructures, and better combinations of mechanical and functional properties than alloys developed by trial and error.
The method's effectiveness depends on the accuracy of the thermodynamic databases.
Complex multicomponent systems may require experimental validation after computational screening.
The exact quantitative improvements in phase stability and material properties are system-dependent and require further study.
